purpose: The Aphrodite showcase example bank: anonymized, behavior-faithful worked examples of what the plugin does to real tool output. Every entry carries the real BEHAVIOR shape (preview line, marker, retrieval round-trip) dressed in GENERIC developer content - no names, no usernames, no secrets, no real paths, no real session ids, no dates, no identifiable project content.
provenance: Shapes extracted from the live plugin runtime (aphrodite.toml defaults, the enriched preview catalog, the marker-format contract, the tool-relay callback flow, the directive injection mechanics) and anonymized. The authored examples below are generic reconstructions, not verbatim captures of any session.

authoringRules.preview: Preview lines marked corpus=true are byte-identical to the Enriched Preview Catalog in docs/proxy/compression.md and the preview-forms block in Site/Source/Content/Docs/guides/hermes-tool-output-schemas.md, so a page may render them verbatim and Drift-Guard's showcase-line check passes. Preview lines marked corpus=false are faithful fragments with varied generic numbers: if a page renders one verbatim, first add it to the docs catalog (or render it as a fragment, not a quote).
authoringRules.hashes: All hashes are fabricated 40-hex placeholders. They are never real content digests.
authoringRules.never: auth.json, .env, and private vault material was never read and never appears here.

examples.title: Cargo build with one compile error
examples.raw:
Compiling app-core v0.1.0 (/home/dev/project/crates/app-core)
error[E0432]: unresolved import `app_core::config`
 --> crates/app-core/src/lib.rs:4:5
  |
4 | use app_core::config;
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ no `config` in the root

warning: unused import: `std::collections::HashMap`
 --> crates/app-core/src/util.rs:2:5
  |
2 | use std::collections::HashMap;
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

error: could not compile `app-core` (lib) due to 1 previous error
examples.note: The preview leads with the tallies (error lines counted line-by-line, never substring matches) and surfaces the first real error message, so the model can act on the failure without retrieving. The warning is counted even though the error is the headline.

examples.title: Clean build is left raw (CLASSIFIER_SKIP)
examples.raw:
Compiling app v0.1.0 (/home/dev/project/crates/app)
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2.41s
examples.note: A build with zero errors and zero warnings is inert: it stays in context untouched and no marker is stored. The preview above is the complete story the classifier would tell, but the skip gate means even that line is unnecessary - the raw two lines cost less than the machinery.

examples.title: Test suite run, all green
examples.raw:
running 220 tests
test result: ok. 220 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; finished in 0.31s
examples.note: Test output gets its own semantic arm (detected by running/test line prefixes even when the classifier only reached the generic terminal bucket). Pass/fail/ignored tallies plus the duration in the preview mean a green run rarely needs retrieval.

examples.title: Test suite run with a failure
examples.raw:
running 48 tests
test config::tests::loads_overrides ... FAILED

test result: FAILED. 47 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; finished in 0.12s
examples.note: On failure the preview swaps the duration for the FAIL'ing test name - the single fact the next action (open the test, fix the assertion) needs. Fragment with varied numbers; not in the docs catalog.

examples.title: Shell command output with its exit code
examples.raw:
cargo build --release 2>&1 | tail -n 20
   Compiling app v0.1.0
    Finished `release` profile target(s) in 18.03s
EXIT:0
examples.note: Terminal output over the terminal threshold (1024 bytes) compresses to a line that keeps the exit code and line count. Under the session rules the exit code - not the prose - is the source of truth, so the model branches on exit=0 without retrieving.

examples.title: Failing shell command keeps its context
examples.raw:
./scripts/migrate.sh
ERROR: migration 004 failed: relation "audit_log" already exists
EXIT:1
examples.note: Same shape, nonzero exit: the preview still shows only line count and exit code. The lesson is the session rule it encodes - never infer success by scanning human-readable text; a nonzero exit code is the retrieval trigger. Fragment with varied numbers; not in the docs catalog.

examples.title: Rust source file structure map
examples.note: The hook/FFI pipeline layout: marker line first, then the structure-map preview (function count, struct count, first signature), then a [meta:] line. Code types sit in the Code tier, so their threshold is the base multiplied by code_multiplier (3.0) - source code gets more headroom before compression than logs of the same size.

examples.title: Python module structure map
examples.note: Per-language code templates swap the fields: classes instead of structs for Python. The first signature in the preview is a real callable signature, so the model can reason about the API without opening the file. Fragment; not in the docs catalog.

examples.title: Ripgrep search across the tree
examples.note: The grep arm counts hits and distinct files and carries the first location, so the model can decide to retrieve (it needs the matching lines) or to just re-run a narrower grep. A zero-match search stays raw - the empty result IS the answer.

examples.title: git status with a dirty tree
examples.raw:
On branch main
Changes not staged for commit:
	modified:   src/main.rs
	modified:   src/lib.rs

Untracked files:

examples.note: Diff previews name the changed files and the plus/minus tallies. The model reviews shape first (how many files, how big) and retrieves only when it must read the actual hunks - e.g. before writing a review comment.

examples.title: A JSON API response
examples.note: JSON lists show item counts, JSON objects show key counts. Note the deliberate exclusion: a wrapper envelope carrying output/exit_code/success keys is NOT re-tagged as json - its raw-JSON preview survives, because that envelope is the tool contract the model needs to read.

examples.title: A running server's log tail
examples.raw:
[INFO] server listening on 127.0.0.1:8080
[DEBUG] connection accepted from 10.0.0.4
[WARN] slow query: 1240ms /api/report
[ERROR] upstream timeout after 30s
[INFO] retry scheduled in 2s
examples.note: Log detection is marker-based: bracketed INFO/WARN/ERROR/DEBUG levels or timestamp-shaped lines. The preview tallies entries, errors and warnings - a quiet log is visible at a glance, and the interesting lines are one retrieve away.

examples.title: Tool relay: async call with a callback URL
examples.note: A callback_url turns the synchronous relay call into a fire-and-forget: an immediate queued reply, then the real result POSTed to the callback (https only, 5s timeout, no auth on the callback POST). Only the aphrodite_* relay tools are accepted; anything else is an error. The result itself is compact metadata, so it stays raw through the hook pipeline.

examples.title: The per-turn directive block
examples.raw:
pre_llm_call, turn 14, injected context (budget 2600 chars):

[directives: focus | foresight]
Aphrodite directives - one primary action per turn; resolve the markers
the next action depends on; prefetch what turn 15 will need.

[nudge: 3 unresolved markers from turn 13]
[recall: 2 entries match this turn's files]

Sections drop bottom-up when over budget; directives and nudges never drop.
examples.note: Directives are short behavioral .md files injected verbatim every turn, placed at the top of the injected context ahead of nudges and the recall catalog. The active set starts as [focus, foresight] and can be swapped mid-session via aphrodite_directive('swap', 'explore') - no config edit. The recall catalog is the first section sacrificed when the 2600-char flow budget is tight.

examples.title: Chain splitting a compound command
examples.raw:
cd project && cargo build --release && cargo test 2>&1
   Compiling app v0.1.0
    Finished `release` profile target(s) in 18.03s

running 220 tests
test result: ok. 220 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0.31s
examples.marker:
cd project && cargo build --release && cargo test
[chain: segments=3]
<<<CCR:e7c0f3a6d9b2e5c8f1a4d7b0c3f6e9a2d5b8c1f479|terminal|398>>>
--- per-segment markers ---
<<<CCR:f8a1...|build_output|210>>>
<<<CCR:a9b2...|test|188>>>
examples.note: Opt-in (chain_split=false by default, because invisible segment markers pollute redirected stdout). With it on, a command with enough segments is rewritten so each segment's output compresses into its own marker - the model sees one build preview and one test preview instead of one blob. Constructs that would corrupt control flow (heredocs, loops spanning segments) are left untouched. Fragment; not in the docs catalog.

examples.title: What stays raw vs compressed at the defaults
examples.raw:
Defaults in play (aphrodite.toml):
  tool_threshold_token = 512      (token proxy: compress above 512 bytes)
  tool_threshold_cache = 4096     (cache proxy: compress above 4096 bytes)
  terminal_threshold   = 1024     (terminal hook: compress above 1024 bytes)
  inline_threshold     = 2048     (above this, store instead of inline zlib)
  code_multiplier      = 3.0      (code tier: base threshold x 3)
  engine_threshold_pct = 45       (context compression engages at 45% fill)

Same 600-byte module docstring:
  - through the token proxy (512): COMPRESSED to a marker
  - through the cache proxy (4096): stays RAW
  - as source code (tier 512 x 3.0 = 1536): stays RAW
examples.note: The tier lesson: whether a given output compresses depends on which surface sees it. The token proxy is aggressive (512), the cache proxy tolerant (4096), terminal output has its own gate (1024), code gets 3x headroom, and the generic fallback preview is the only thing a text blob shows. Essential tools (read_file, memory, skill_view...) and the aphrodite_* tools themselves are always raw regardless of size.

examples.title: Below threshold: raw; at threshold: marker
examples.raw: src/preview.rs:12:pub fn build_preview(content: &str, kind: Kind) -> String {
examples.note: A one-line grep result is far under every threshold: it passes through untouched, no marker, no storage. The same search across a large tree (the grep-search example) crosses the line and becomes a marker. Compression is never a judgment call - it is a byte count against the surface's threshold.
